title: Nuelments: A Shopify Store Design and Development Case Study for an Indian Hair Care Brand
storyLead: How Teknoppy built a problem-led Shopify store for an Indian hair care brand, helping shoppers dealing with hair fall, dandruff and hard water damage find the right product, see it in use and check out in a few taps.
atAGlance: Nuelments sells a focused range of hair care products, from onion and biotin shampoo to a rosemary hair serum and biotin gummies
Every product is one click from the main menu, so shoppers find what they need without searching
A problem-led section speaks directly to itchy, flaky scalps and links each concern to a product
Shoppable "Shop the Look" videos show products in use and let shoppers buy straight from the video
Ingredient badges, a first-order offer, quick view and Buy Now buttons make the path to checkout short and confident
aboutParagraphs: Nuelments is an Indian hair care brand built on the idea of combining science and nature. Its products are made in India and sold directly to customers through its own online store, with prices in Indian rupees.

The range covers six products: an Onion and Biotin Shampoo and Conditioner, an Advanced Hair Growth Serum with aloe vera and rosemary oil, Biotin Plus Gummies, a Hard Water Protection Co-Wash and an Anti Dandruff Hair Mask. Sale prices run from Rs. 199 to Rs. 449, positioning Nuelments as an accessible everyday brand rather than a luxury label.

The products are designed for common Indian hair concerns: hair fall, dandruff, dry and damaged hair, curly hair and the effects of hard water. The store displays badges such as Paraben Free, Sulphate Free, Cruelty Free, Non-Comedogenic, Dermatologically Tested and Made in India. Teknoppy was brought in to design and build a beauty brand website on Shopify that turns this range into a simple, trustworthy shopping experience.
challengeLead: Five problems shaped the store design.

challenges.title: A crowded hair care category
challenges.description: Indian shoppers can choose from many onion, biotin and rosemary products. A new D2C brand needs a clear reason to be chosen.

challenges.title: Shoppers start with a problem, not a product
challenges.description: People search for "hair fall" or "dandruff", not a product name. The store had to connect problems to products quickly.

challenges.title: Trust in ingredients
challenges.description: Beauty buyers read labels carefully. They want to know what is in a product, and what is not, before they buy.

challenges.title: Seeing is believing
challenges.description: Photos alone don't show texture, application or results. Shoppers want to see products being used.

challenges.title: Mobile-first, impulse-friendly buying
challenges.description: Many beauty shoppers buy on their phones, where every extra step between interest and checkout can lose a sale.

objectiveLead: The goal was a fast, trustworthy hair care ecommerce website that helps Indian shoppers find the right product and buy with confidence.
objectives: Put every product one click from the main menu
Connect common hair and scalp problems to the right product
Show products in use through shoppable video
Make ingredients and quality badges visible on the homepage
Shorten the path from product view to checkout on mobile
approachLead: Six decisions that take a shopper from concern to checkout in a few taps.

approachPillars.title: A menu that is the catalogue
paragraphs: With a focused range, the main menu lists each product type directly: Hair Conditioner, Hair Shampoo, Hair Serum, Biotin Plus Gummies, Hair Mask, Co-Wash and Combo Offers. Shoppers reach any product in one tap, with no category maze.

approachPillars.title: Problem-led merchandising
paragraphs: A homepage section headed "Scalp in Distress, Itchy, Flaky, Uneven" speaks to the shopper's concern first, then introduces the product that addresses it. A hero banner leads with biotin for healthy hair.

approachPillars.title: Shoppable "Shop the Look" videos
paragraphs: Short videos show the products being used, with each product tagged so shoppers can add it to their cart directly from the video, bringing a social-media style experience into the store.

approachPillars.title: Ingredient and quality badges
paragraphs: An "Our Certifications" section and product badges highlight what matters to label readers, such as Paraben Free, Sulphate Free, Cruelty Free, Dermatologically Tested and Made in India.

approachPillars.title: Fewer steps to checkout
paragraphs: Quick view, Buy Now, wishlist and compare features let shoppers decide from the product grid, and digital wallet checkout shortens payment on mobile. Search suggests trending terms to speed up discovery.

approachPillars.title: Offers that start a relationship
paragraphs: A first-order discount banner and a newsletter sign-up with an introductory offer turn first-time visitors into subscribers and repeat buyers.

deliverables.description: Every product reachable from the main menu.

whyMattersHeading: Why Problem-Led Shopify Design Wins D2C Beauty Shoppers in India
whyMattersParagraphs: Many Indian D2C beauty brands grow through Instagram and short video. Shoppers discover a product in a reel, then visit the brand's store to decide. A Shopify store that feels as visual and fast as social media, with shoppable videos and one-tap buying, keeps that momentum instead of losing it.
Problem-first design matters because hair care is personal. Leading with the concern, then the solution, builds the kind of trust that turns a first order into a repeat purchase.

Transparency closes the sale, especially for a cosmetics ecommerce website in India. Clear ingredient badges answer the label reader's questions on the homepage, without forcing them to dig through product pages. For an accessible brand competing on value, that clarity is a real advantage.
whyMattersCalloutHtml: For a D2C beauty brand, the Shopify store should feel like the best moment of a reel: instant, visual and one tap from buying.
